fixes.explanation: Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a big name, so I get why it came to mind. But the writer doesn't say a word about the law of Moses here. He says, “Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God…” (1 John 5:1). Believing is the line he draws, not a checklist.
Right, baker. The writer says, “And His commandments are not burdensome…” (1 John 5:3). Not burdensome means they aren't a heavy load to haul around. He's saying they don't weigh you down.

Yes, baker. The writer gives the reason right away: “…because everyone born of God overcomes the world.” (1 John 5:4). Verse 3 says the commandments aren't burdensome, and verse 4 says why. Those born of God overcome the world, so the commandments don't weigh them down.

That's right, baker. The writer asks who overcomes the world, then answers: “Only he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God.” (1 John 5:5). Notice the question comes right after he calls our faith the victory in verse 4. So the one who overcomes is the one who believes.

The writer says the reverse, baker. He says, “Even if we accept human testimony, the testimony of God is greater.” (1 John 5:9). Greater, not harder to trust. In the very next verse he says whoever does not believe God has made Him out to be a liar (1 John 5:10).
